drafts.title: Center screen and head‑up remain legible in bright sunlight and against glare
drafts.description: When driving in bright daylight the driver can read critical information on the center screen and the head‑up display (HUD) without needing to shade the screen or squint.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In a daylight usability test (ambient illuminance up to 10,000 lux, typical midday sun), 90% of drivers must be able to correctly read and interpret 8 standardized on‑screen or HUD items (navigation turn, speed, media title, warning icon, climate status, lane guidance, incoming call ID, and an active route instruction) within 2 seconds from normal seated position and ±15° head yaw.
assumptions: Test uses a panel of 30 representative drivers wearing typical sunglasses and without sunglasses in randomized trials.
Measurement method follows an agreed UX lab procedure that reproduces real sun angles and reflections (up to 10,000 lux).
Automatic brightness/contrast adaptations and anti‑reflective treatments are enabled by default.
uncertainties: Extreme glare situations above 10,000 lux (e.g., snow glare) may still reduce legibility.
Legibility may vary with aftermarket window films or extreme tinted sunglasses.

drafts.title: Physical climate controls that can be operated without looking
drafts.description: Drivers can change temperature and fan speed by touch alone so they do not need to look away from the road to operate climate controls.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In usability testing, 90% of drivers must be able to (a) increase or decrease cabin temperature by 3°C and (b) change fan speed by two levels using only tactile controls within 3 seconds per action from the driving seating position.
assumptions: Controls include distinct tactile elements (knobs, ridged buttons, or haptic switches) laid out logically within reach.
Users perform tests on a parked vehicle replicating seated driving posture; testers wear typical driving gloves in a subset of trials.
uncertainties: Different hand sizes and gloves may affect speed and accuracy in edge cases.
Some climate features may remain only in the touchscreen for efficiency reasons.

drafts.title: Voice control reliably understands and executes common driving commands
drafts.description: While driving, drivers can use natural voice to control navigation, media, phone and climate and expect consistent recognition and execution.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In a mixed‑noise cabin test (background noise up to 75 dB(A)), the voice system must correctly recognize and execute at least 95% of a 50‑command test set (common driving commands for navigation, media, phone, and climate) across 30 drivers with varied accents.
assumptions: Test command set is defined from field usage data and includes synonyms (e.g., 'navigate home', 'find home').
Evaluation counts successful end‑state (action completed) rather than exact transcript match.
Tests include voice input with typical in‑car audio (radio/music) and realistic road noise.
uncertainties: Performance may vary with very strong regional accents or non‑native speakers.
Privacy or connectivity settings (cloud vs local processing) may affect latency or accuracy.

drafts.title: Wireless charging pad reliably starts and maintains charging for common phones
drafts.description: When a supported phone is placed on the wireless charging pad it starts charging automatically and continues charging reliably during typical driving use.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Across 10 popular phone models (representing iOS and Android shapes/sizes) and 100 standardized placement trials, the wireless pad must begin charging within 5 seconds of placement and maintain uninterrupted charging for at least 95 of 100 trials for the duration of a 15‑minute drive segment.
assumptions: Trials include phones with thin cases (≤3 mm) and typical in‑pocket dirt exposure scenarios; very thick or magnetic cases are excluded from pass/fail counts.
Phone battery states at start of trial vary (10–80%) to reflect real world usage.
uncertainties: Some phone models with unusual coil placement or heavy metal cases may still have intermittent contact.
Aftermarket accessories or badly aligned placement by users will increase failure rate.

drafts.title: Heated steering wheel included as part of the Cold Weather package
drafts.description: Customers who select the Cold Weather package receive a heated steering wheel as part of that package, reducing the need to buy it separately.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: For all vehicle orders that include the Cold Weather package, the delivered vehicle must include a heated steering wheel in 100% of cases (checked on a sample of 500 production vehicles).
assumptions: Cold Weather package content is communicated clearly in configurator and dealer order systems.
This applies to the U.S. market launch; regional package contents may vary in other markets per local requirements.
uncertainties: Some legacy hardware variants or steering wheel trims might require a short lead time to include by default.
Customers who previously purchased steering wheel options separately may expect credits; incentives are a separate commercial decision.

drafts.title: Requests for lower base price, cheaper leases, subscription pricing and financing offers (pricing and commercial requests)
drafts.description: Customers asked for lower base price, cheaper lease rates versus competitors, free option packages, 30% discounts on Comfort package, lower dealer margins on extras, $15/month heated seats subscription and 0% financing.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Commercial and pricing requests are acknowledged and tracked for regional product & sales decisions; these items are outside the product requirement scope and will be handled by BMW Sales/Finance teams.
assumptions: Pricing, lease rates, subscriptions and dealer margins are decisions made by commercial and finance organizations, not engineering product requirements.
uncertainties: The level of interest in specific commercial schemes may vary by market and over time.
drafts.scope_reason: Pricing, financing and subscription fees are commercial decisions or business case items and outside the product requirement scope.

drafts.title: Request that infotainment meets Chinese CCC certification
drafts.description: Customers asked the infotainment system to pass Chinese CCC certification for sale in China.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Request logged for regional compliance program; certification and homologation activities are managed by regulatory/compliance teams and are out of scope for product UX requirements.
assumptions: Homologation and certification are handled by dedicated regulatory teams and depend on regional legal requirements.
uncertainties: Specific technical changes required by certification are undefined in customer feedback and may affect product design later.
drafts.scope_reason: Certification/homologation is a regulatory activity outside product UX requirement scope.

drafts.title: Request that driver profile satisfies GDPR requirements
drafts.description: Customers asked that the driver profile and related data storage satisfy GDPR requirements.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Request captured and passed to Data Protection & Legal teams; GDPR compliance and legal obligations are out of scope for product feature requirements.
assumptions: Legal and data‑protection requirements are implemented by the privacy/compliance organization; product UX teams will coordinate as needed.
uncertainties: GDPR implementation details (e.g., export/delete flows) are not specified by the signal and may produce additional product requirements after legal review.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulatory/legal compliance (GDPR) is handled by Legal/Privacy and is out of scope for product requirement drafting.

drafts.title: Request for a specific cockpit compute chip (Snapdragon 8295)
drafts.description: Customers requested that the cockpit computer uses the Snapdragon 8295 chip.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Request documented and forwarded to platform/architecture teams; selection of specific silicon is an engineering specification and outside the product requirements scope.
assumptions: Component selection (chipsets) is an engineering/architecture decision based on power, performance, cost and supplier strategy.
uncertainties: Customer preference for a chip does not guarantee availability, supplier approval, or fit with system architecture.
drafts.scope_reason: Specification of a specific chip is an engineering decision and out of scope for customer-facing product requirements.
